chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام:
About a man who swears an oath and forgets what he said. He said: “It is according to what he intended.”

key_terms.يَحْلِفُ: he swears or takes an oath

ai.seo_question: If someone swears an oath and then forgets the exact words, is it judged by the wording or by the intention?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about an oath whose wording is later forgotten by the one who made it. The ruling is that the oath is judged according to the person’s intention, showing the importance of niyyah in legal and moral responsibility.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4303 - Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as)

about a man who takes an oath and then forgets what he said.
Imam (as) replied: "It is based on what he intended."
